top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is one sharply defined invention (magic-wavelength trapping that cancels the light shift for many atoms at once) with a measured, reproduced result near 1e-18 across several laboratories, and all eight members name the same two laureates, so allocation and citation scope are clean. It is not a refinement of the comb or ion-control prizes. P001 is a close second: the flat-band prediction followed by experiment is the cleanest prediction-then-discovery sequence on the list and opens a broad field, but the nature of the superconductivity and several correlated states is still contested and experimental credit cannot be fully captured by three names. Either is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; she is a theoretical atomic physicist with no documented tie to Katori or Ye, and her documented collaborators (L'Huillier, Keller, Lund, Schuch, Dahlstrom, Argenti, Indelicato) are not among the P001 or P002 laureates
